Voxel Chunk Management handles the storage, state tracking, and dirty-flag propagation for a fixed-size 3D block of voxel data within a sparse voxel architecture [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly describes a system that manages a 3D block of voxel data (voxels: ndarray of Uint16Array with shape [size, size, size]). It details the allocation of this array, the tracking of neighbor references (_neighbors), and the management of dirty flags (_terrainDirty/_objectsDirty). The code snippets demonstrate the logic for setting voxel IDs, updating dirty flags, and propagating dirtiness to edge neighbors (chunk boundaries) to trigger remeshing. This aligns perfectly with the claim's description of handling storage, state tracking, and dirty-flag propagation for a fixed-size 3D block within a sparse voxel architecture.

It solves the problem of efficiently determining when a chunk's geometric representation or logical state requires regeneration after voxel modifications, specifically by isolating boundary updates to prevent cascading recomputations across the voxel grid [S1, unofficial].

It further provides code logic that checks boundary conditions (`i===0`, `i===edge`, etc.) to propagate dirtiness only to edge neighbors. This directly supports the claim that the system isolates boundary updates to prevent cascading recomputations.
